Application Materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Degree transcripts.** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year.
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. Please note that original documentation will be required before you enrol. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- **Referee details.** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. A reference provided by email must be sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as 'Yahoo' or 'Hotmail' are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose.** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable).** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof. Please see the [English Language Requirements](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/) section for more details.
You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. Once you have received evidence of obtaining your qualifications you can upload them to the MySIS Applicant portal. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **UK degree requirements:** A **2:1 or above** at undergraduate level in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Mathematics or a related discipline.
- **Other routes:** Applicants with a good **2:2 degree (55% or above)** will be considered on an individual basis.
- **China applicants:** We normally consider the following qualifications for entry to our postgraduate taught programmes: **Bachelor Degree (minimum 4 years) from selected institutions**. **UK 1st class degree:** 85 to 95%; **UK 2:1 degree:** 70 to 80%; **UK 2:2 degree:** 65 to 75%. Offer conditions will vary depending on the institution you are applying from.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language requirements for Queen Mary programmes are indicated by English bands, and the specific test and score acceptable is based on the band assigned to the academic department within which the chosen course is administered. The English Language requirements for entry to postgraduate taught and research programmes in the School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science falls within:
- **Band 4:** IELTS (Academic) minimum score **6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking**.
- Queen Mary accepts a range of English tests and qualifications categorised in English bands to demonstrate English Language proficiency. See [all accepted English tests](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/) deemed equivalent to these IELTS scores.

Program Overview.content:
Machine Learning for Visual Data Analytics MSc is part of AI, Computer and Data Science. As recent developments in computers and sensors make the generation, storage and processing of visual data easier, methods that enable a machine to analyse and understand images and videos become increasingly relevant. This programme is designed to train engineers to work in the analysis and interpretation of images and video.
- Undertake high-level training in programming languages, tools and methods necessary for the design and implementation of practical computer vision systems.
- Be taught by world-class researchers in the fields of multimedia analysis, vision-based surveillance, structure from motion and human motion analysis.
- Work on cutting-edge research projects, gaining hands-on experience.
- Study options include full-time September 2026 | 1 year, part-time September 2026 | 2 years, and full-time September 2027 | 1 year. Location: Mile End.
This course will enable students to study cutting-edge technologies in the field of machine learning for visual analytics, and will provide them with the background and skills they need to pursue careers in research or industry. Course content covers fundamental methods and techniques in computer vision, machine learning and image processing; programming tools, languages and techniques for the application of machine learning methods to analyse visual data; and methods and techniques for systems and applications.
The programme is taught by academics from the Computer Vision and Multimedia and Vision research groups. The groups consist of a team of more than 100 researchers (academics, post-docs, research fellows and PhD students) performing world-leading research into the fields of surveillance, face and gesture recognition, multimedia indexing and retrieval and robotics. The School has collaborations, partnerships, industrial placement schemes and public engagement programmes with organisations including Vodafone, Google, IBM, BT, NASA, BBC and Microsoft.
This degree is accredited by [BCS](https://heaccreditation.bcs.org/), The Chartered Institute for IT, for the purposes of partially meeting the academic requirement for registration as a Chartered IT Professional. This degree is also accredited by [BCS](https://heaccreditation.bcs.org/) on behalf of the [Engineering Council](https://www.engc.org.uk/education-skills/course-search/recognised-course-search/), for the purposes of partially meeting the academic requirement for registration as a Chartered Engineer.
Structure:
- Eight modules divided into two streams; students choose **one** stream to follow once they start in September.
- Compulsory final project module (60 credits).
- Streams include Vision and Language, and Computer Vision and Image Processing. These streams will allow you to further develop your professional profile and graduate with industry-relevant expertise.
Assessment:
- 67% Modules
- 33% Research project
- Modules are assessed through a combination of coursework and written examinations. You will also be assessed through your final research project.
You will devise and carry out a major final project, which you may do in collaboration with an industrial partner. Examples of past project topics include automatic road segmentation, sponsored by Yamaha Motors Ltd.; 3D face reconstruction from a few images; and sentiment analysis in images.
Students of this course can expect to take part in lectures, in which the theory and algorithms are presented, and practical sessions and labs, where they can get hands-on experience with tools and algorithms. Each module provides contact time with your lecturers, supported by lab work and self-directed further study. You will be assigned an Academic Advisor who will guide you in both academic and pastoral matters throughout your time at Queen Mary. Part-time study options often mean that the number of modules taken is reduced per semester, with the full modules required to complete the programme spread over two academic years.
Faculty include [Professor Shaogang Gong](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/gongshaogang.html), Professor of Visual Computation, whose research focuses on object recognition, action and behaviour recognition, and video analysis; [Dr Miles Hansard](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/hansardmiles.html), whose research interests cover statistical scene and image models, depth-cameras and multi-view scene reconstruction, binocular vision, eye-movements and 3D displays; [Professor Ioannis Patras](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/patrasioannis.html), Professor of Computer Vision and Human Sensing, whose research focuses on analysis of human behaviour, emotions and cognitive states from images, video and their neurophysiological signals; [Professor Massimo Poesio](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/poesiomassimo.html), Professor of Computational Linguistics; [Dr Paulo Rauber](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/rauberpaulo.html), Lecturer in Artificial Intelligence; and [Dr Fabrizio Smeraldi](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/smeraldifabrizio.html), Senior Lecturer in Artificial Intelligence.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s main [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital. The School has bespoke facilities including the newly refurbished [Informatics Laboratory (ITL)](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/about-us/facilities/informatics-teaching-laboratory---itl--facilities/), transformed through a £20 million investment; Augmented human interaction (AHI) laboratory; Antenna measurement laboratory; qMedia and arts technology studios; Robotics laboratory (ARQspace); and Dedicated Postgraduate Teaching Facilities.
Career paths: skills and knowledge in intelligent image and video processing are valuable across industries including multimedia indexing and retrieval, motion capture, media production, medical imaging, security and defense, and robotics. Expertise in machine learning, signal processing, and programming is highly sought after in various other industries. Many faculty members collaborate on research projects with industry partners, including Disney, BBC, Technicolor, and STMicroelectronics, and also engage in consultancy work. You will be well-prepared to pursue further research or PhD studies. **100%** in highly skilled jobs 15 months after graduation.

This course will enable students to study cutting-edge technologies in the field of machine learning for visual analytics. Course content covers:

Structure:
- Eight modules divided into two streams; students choose **one** stream to follow once they start in September.
- Compulsory final project module (**60 credits**).
Vision and Language stream:
- **Semester 1:** Machine Learning; Introduction to Computer Vision; Applied Statistics; Natural Language Processing.
- **Semester 2:** Deep Learning and Computer Vision; Machine Learning for Visual Data Analysis; Neural Networks and NLP; Neural Networks and Deep Learning.
- **Semester 3:** Project Module.
Computer Vision and Image Processing stream:
- **Semester 1:** Machine Learning; Introduction to Computer Vision; Applied Statistics; Computer Graphics.
- **Semester 2:** Deep Learning and Computer Vision; Machine Learning for Visual Data Analysis; Big Data Processing; Neural Networks and Deep Learning.
- **Semester 3:** Project Module.
Compulsory/Core modules include Neural Networks and Deep Learning, Machine Learning, Introduction to Computer Vision, Project, Applied Statistics, Deep Learning and Computer Vision, and Machine Learning for Visual Data Analysis. Elective modules: _Please note that all modules are subject to change._
Assessment:
- 67% Modules
- 33% Research project
Modules are assessed through a combination of coursework and written examinations. You will also be assessed through your final research project.
Research project: You will devise and carry out a major final project, which you may do in collaboration with an industrial partner. Examples of past project topics include:
- Automatic road segmentation - sponsored by Yamaha Motors Ltd.
- 3D face reconstruction from a few images.
- Sentiment analysis in images.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s main [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/). Students of this course can expect to take part in lectures, and practical sessions and labs. Part-time study options often mean that the number of modules taken is reduced per semester, with the full modules required to complete the programme spread over two academic years.

Financial Aid.content:
Queen Mary is pleased to offer a number of generous scholarships to students on our MSc and PhD programmes:
- **Martingale Scholarship Programme**: The School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science is partnering with the Martingale Foundation to offer postgraduate scholarships in AI for home fee-paying students. Visit the [Martingale Foundation](https://martingale.foundation/) website for application details and deadlines.
- **Global Talent Scholarship**: [The Global Talent Scholarship](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/global-talent-scholarship--postgraduate-taught-september-2026.html) aims to attract talented students from around the world and offers a **£3000 reduction in tuition fees**. Specific criteria need to be met.
- A wide range of other scholarships and bursaries are available to students of all programmes, including the [QMUL Alumni Loyalty Award](http://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/funding_masters/queen-mary-alumni-loyalty-award/) and the UK government's international [Chevening Awards](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/chevening-awards.html). **View all scholarships and bursaries on the [scholarships directory](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/database/).**

Multiple Applications.content:
You may apply for a maximum of two taught programmes or one taught and one research programme at Queen Mary per application cycle. Please note that you can only study for one qualification at a time, so if you receive offers for both programmes you will be required to accept one and decline the other.
Is there an application fee? No, the university does not charge an application fee.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: The withdrawal and deferral process differs depending on your programme level and your enrolment status. Please consider the deferral deadlines published online for [Postgraduate Taught](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/deadlines/) programmes. The [Enrolment FAQs](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/newstudents/faqs/enrolment/) set out in more detail the withdrawal and deferral processes.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. You will receive a conditional offer which will state what qualifications and grades you will need to achieve in order to meet Queen Mary's entry requirements. Once you have received evidence of obtaining your qualifications you can upload them to the [MySIS Applicant portal](https://mysis.qmul.ac.uk/), after which you will receive an unconditional offer once all conditions have been met. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.
